three-notches.title: Three notches, one per whine
three-notches.caption: The laptop design: one narrow dip on each whine pitch, and everything else passes untouched.

hum.title: One click, laptop against chip
hum.caption: The same rule after one click. On the laptop the ring dies; on the chip it grows ×15.8 every 50 samples, then clips on both sides.

coefficients.title: A filter is its coefficients
coefficients.caption: Lesson 6’s notch, one wire per sample. The three numbers in the circles are its coefficients: change a number, change the filter.

chip-steps.title: The chip snaps every coefficient to a tick
chip-steps.caption: Each coefficient is stored as the nearest whole number of steps. One step serves the whole rule, so the biggest coefficient decides how coarse every tick is.

pole-drift.title: Rounding moves the crowded poles
pole-drift.caption: Zoomed on the top of the unit circle. The outer pole pairs cross the rim; lesson 6’s notch, at the same zoom, barely moves.

pile-up.title: Multiplying piles the numbers up
pile-up.caption: Multiply the notches one at a time: the numbers grow like the 1, 3, 3, 1 of (1 + x)³, and none of them is tied to one pole any more.

push.title: Each rounding error pushes each pole
push.caption: Each rounding error pushes each pole, and the pushes add like arrows: the middle pole is pushed in, its neighbors out.

tangent.title: A flat curve slides its crossing far
tangent.caption: Lift a curve by ε and its crossing slides by ε ÷ steepness. Steep: a short slide. Flat: a long one.

crowd.title: Crowded poles have a big multiplier
crowd.caption: The steepness at a pole is the product of the arrows from the other poles to it. Two short arrows make it tiny, and the multiplier huge.

section.title: In a section, every number means something
section.caption: The 1,900 Hz section. Every number is something you can see: the volume, the zeros’ angle and place on the circle, the poles’ angle and radius.

cascade.title: A cascade keeps each pair alone
cascade.caption: The same filter, built as three second-order sections in a row. Each pole pair is rounded on its own and lands at 0.9763.

bits.title: More bits: the multiplied-out rule
bits.caption: The multiplied-out rule needs 13 bits to stay safely inside the circle. The cascade is already at 0.9763 with 8.
